meta.title: Hemodialysis patient missing sessions after selling his car

patient.name: Raymond Ellis
patient.coverage: Lakeshore Community Health Plan (fictional Medicaid MCO)
problems: Type 2 diabetes with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Hypertensive CKD with stage 5 CKD or ESRD

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: The dialysis unit tells me you've missed three sessions this month. What's been going on?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I don't drive anymore. I sold the car in August, couldn't keep up with the insurance.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: How have you been getting to the unit?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two buses, all the way down to Park Manor. That was the only chair they had, three o'clock. I'm out the door by one-thirty, and after four hours on the machine it's two more buses home. I don't get in till eight-thirty. Some days I just don't go.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Is there anyone who can drive you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My daughter's in Indiana. My neighbor helped a couple times but he works days.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Let's talk about food. How are you eating on dialysis days?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Mostly whatever the corner store has. Chips, lunch meat. The real grocery is a bus ride away and I'm wiped out after treatment.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: And the phosphate binder, the sevelamer?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I take it when I eat. If I skip lunch I skip the pill too.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: Any trouble paying for your medicines?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, the copays are a few dollars. That part's fine.

turns.speaker: doctor
turns.text: I'd also like the surgeons to look at your fistula in two weeks.

Daily weight and blood pressure log on paper; bring to each session
